Best Roofing Materials for Your New Roof in Allentown

10 March 2025 Roof InstallationRoofing

Installing a new roof is a major investment for any homeowner. It’s more than just shingles—it’s about protecting your home, boosting energy efficiency, and enhancing curb appeal. But with so many options available, choosing the right materials can feel overwhelming.

If you’re planning a roof replacement or building a new home, this guide will help you select the best roofing materials Allentown homeowners need for long-lasting, reliable protection. Plus, we’ll share expert insights from In The Light Roofing, a trusted local roofing company based in Allentown, PA.

Consider Allentown’s weather conditions when choosing materials

Allentown experiences a variety of weather patterns throughout the year, from freezing winters to hot, humid summers. Your roof needs to handle these extremes without cracking, warping, or losing its protective qualities.

Weather factors to consider:

  • Winter snow and ice: Roofs must support heavy snow loads and resist ice dams.
  • Summer heat and UV exposure: Prolonged sunlight can cause some materials to deteriorate faster.
  • Heavy rain and storms: Strong winds and downpours require durable, water-resistant materials.
  • Seasonal temperature changes: Freeze-thaw cycles can cause some materials to expand and contract, leading to cracks.

Working with a local expert like In The Light Roofing ensures you get materials suited to Allentown’s climate.

Evaluate the durability and lifespan of roofing materials

Durability matters when investing in a new roof. Some materials last decades with minimal upkeep, while others need regular maintenance to stay in good condition.

Durable roofing materials for Allentown homes:

  • Asphalt shingles: Last 20–30 years and offer solid weather resistance.
  • Metal roofing: Can last 40–70 years with minimal maintenance.
  • Slate tiles: Extremely durable, with a lifespan of 75+ years.
  • Wood shakes: Beautiful but require more upkeep and last 20–30 years.

Choosing a long-lasting material can save money over time by reducing the need for repairs and replacements.

Understand the energy efficiency of different roofing materials

Energy-efficient roofing helps lower utility bills by reducing heat transfer through the roof. In Allentown, this is especially important given the hot summers and cold winters.

Energy-efficient roofing options:

  • Metal roofs: Reflect sunlight and reduce cooling costs.
  • Cool asphalt shingles: Coated to reflect more heat than standard shingles.
  • Clay tiles: Naturally insulating and help regulate indoor temperatures.
  • Green roofs: Covered with vegetation to provide excellent insulation.

Ask your contractor about energy-efficient options that qualify for potential tax credits or rebates. For more details, check out our New Roof Installation page.

Think about the aesthetic appeal and curb value

Your roof is a significant part of your home’s exterior. The right material can enhance your property’s look and increase its market value.

Popular roofing styles in Allentown:

  • Architectural asphalt shingles: Mimic wood or slate while being cost-effective.
  • Metal panels: Provide a sleek, modern appearance.
  • Slate tiles: Add timeless charm and elegance.
  • Cedar shakes: Create a rustic, natural look.

In The Light Roofing can help you choose materials that complement your home’s style and neighborhood.

Weigh the maintenance requirements for each material

All roofs need maintenance, but some materials require more care than others. Understanding the upkeep requirements helps you choose a material that fits your lifestyle and budget.

Maintenance considerations:

  • Asphalt shingles: Low maintenance but prone to granule loss over time.
  • Metal roofing: Requires occasional inspections for dents or corrosion.
  • Slate tiles: Durable but need professionals for repairs.
  • Wood shakes: Need regular treatment to resist rot and insect damage.

Choosing low-maintenance materials can save time and money in the long run.

Factor in the cost and long-term value

Roofing materials come with different price tags. While it’s tempting to choose the cheapest option, investing in high-quality materials often pays off with fewer repairs and a longer lifespan.

Cost factors to consider:

  • Material price: Asphalt is the most affordable; slate is the most expensive.
  • Installation complexity: Some materials, like slate, take longer to install, increasing labor costs.
  • Long-term value: Metal and slate offer better durability, reducing long-term expenses.
  • Energy savings: Energy-efficient materials lower heating and cooling costs.

Get a detailed, written estimate from a trusted contractor like In The Light Roofing before making a final decision.

Consider environmental impact and sustainability

Eco-friendly roofing materials help reduce your home’s environmental footprint. With increasing focus on sustainable building practices, many homeowners are now choosing materials that are recyclable or made from natural sources.

Sustainable roofing options:

  • Metal roofing: 100% recyclable at the end of its lifespan.
  • Clay and slate tiles: Made from natural materials with minimal processing.
  • Cool roofs: Reflect sunlight, reducing urban heat island effects.
  • Recycled shingles: Made from recycled rubber or plastic materials.

Ask about environmentally friendly options when discussing your project with your roofing contractor.

Hire a professional roofing contractor for proper installation

Even the best materials won’t perform well if they’re installed incorrectly. Proper installation ensures maximum durability, energy efficiency, and weather protection.

What to look for in a roofing contractor:

  • Local experience: Knowledge of Allentown’s climate and building codes.
  • Proper licensing and insurance: Protects you during the project.
  • Proven track record: Positive reviews and completed projects in the area.
  • Clear communication: Honest answers about materials, costs, and timelines.

Frequently asked questions

What is the most popular roofing material in Allentown?

Asphalt shingles remain the most popular choice due to their affordability, durability, and variety of styles.

How can I choose the best roofing materials for energy efficiency?

Metal roofs, cool asphalt shingles, and clay tiles are great for energy efficiency. These materials reflect heat and improve indoor comfort.

Does Allentown’s weather affect roofing material choices?

Absolutely. Our cold winters, hot summers, and frequent rainstorms make it essential to choose weather-resistant materials.

How long does a typical roof last in Allentown?

Asphalt shingles last 20–30 years, while metal roofs can last 40–70 years. Slate tiles can last over a century with proper care.

What should I look for when hiring a roofing contractor?

Choose a licensed, insured contractor with local experience and positive reviews. Visit our New Roof Installation page to see what we offer.

Where can I find expert roof installation services in Allentown?
